title: Nautilus Prioritized Roadmap (Gap-Hardening)
content: Nautilus Prioritized Roadmap (Gap-Hardening) R0 — Release blockers Deterministic install profile under restricted/proxy networks Scope: preinstall/tooling dependency behavior, local fallback contract, contributor docs. Exit: npm ci failure modes classified and documented; deterministic fallback command validated. Bound default test runtime Scope: split long-running suites from default npm test ; enforce runtime ceilings. Exit: default test command completes deterministically in CI/local target windows. R1 — Hardening Remote execution/probe trust-boundary hardening matrix (deny-by-default regression coverage). Canonical contract ownership lint checks across runtime/plugin/blueprint seams. Receipt truth hardening (real timing fields, degraded cause taxonomy consistency). R2 — Performance / Model routing Deterministic scheduler v2 scoring: VRAM capacity, queue pressure, context budget, observed latency. Local capability telemetry bridge into registry snapshots. Load-shedding + bounded queue admission with explicit degraded outputs. R3 — UX / Operator console Receipt-backed runtime timeline (decision reasons, fallback attempts, degraded transitions). “Why this model/provider” explainer panel sourced from canonical receipt fields. First-run readiness checks for local inference/provider policy setup. R4 — Multi-agent / Context efficiency Handoff packet schema and replayable artifact summaries. Context compaction policy with token budget thresholds. Duplicate-work prevention via execution memory fingerprints. R5 — Future-proof platform features Operator proofpack bundles with replay/export parity checks. Benchmark harness for routing policy calibration (latency/cost/context fit). Optional distributed worker seam (explicitly unsupported until contracts + trust model stabilize). Dependency ordering R0 must complete before deeper hardening/performance work to preserve deterministic release confidence. R1 contract hardening should land before R2 optimization to avoid optimizing unstable boundaries. R3 and R4 can progress in parallel once receipt/event schema stability is achieved in R1. Status update (2026-05-22) R0.2 (bounded default test path): implemented ( npm test => npm run test:unit ; npm run test:full opt-in). R0.1 (restricted install resilience): partially addressed via explicit degraded local bootstrap contract ( npm ci --ignore-scripts ) while preserving fail-closed CI semantics. Status update (2026-05-22, implementation batch) R1: partial+ (hardening utilities implemented with focused tests; broader trust-boundary matrix and contract-ownership lint still pending). R4: implemented core primitives (handoff schema validation, context compaction, fingerprints/reuse guard, token budget overflow degrade, checkpoint shape + replay helpers). R5: implemented core governance/evidence (queue admission/idempotency/retry/dead-letter/load-shed timeline, proofpack evidence builder, release gate waiver logic, benchmark harness unavailable/latency behavior, verification matrix script-existence check
summary: Deterministic install profile under restricted/proxy networks
